_transcription: ENGLISH half only. 23 rendered pages. Bilingual with Hindi and English on ALTERNATING pages, Hindi FIRST: idx 0 = cover, idx 1 = Hindi General Instructions, idx 2 = English General Instructions + Q1, then Hindi/English pairs throughout. English pages are therefore the EVEN 0-based indices 2..22 — the alternating hypothesis HELD, same as 65/2/1. Section A on idx 2/4/6/8/10, B on 12, C on 14, D on 16, E on 18/20/22. All 20 Section-A answers are CBSE's own, read verbatim off the marking scheme for this exact paper code (65/2/2, ms/p02..p06); my own derivation agreed with the key on all 20, so no disagreement flags. Every one of the 14 questions NOT shared with 65/2/1 was additionally cross-checked against the marking scheme, which reprints each question block above its solution — all 14 matched my transcription of the question paper. Decimal points are printed as RAISED dots (0·00001%, -0·01) and are written {\cdot}. MCQ option labels are UPPERCASE (A)-(D); internal-choice sub-labels are lowercase (a)/(b). 'Case Study - 1/2/3' headings ARE printed and are recorded in _caseStudyLabel, never in context; on THIS set the dash is an EN DASH (verified by cropping the heading at 5x — it is visibly wider than a hyphen), whereas the committed 65/2/1 file stores an ASCII hyphen. _caseStudyLabel is provenance and is not hashed, so this does not affect dedup. Case Study 1 (Q36, the LPP/diet passage) has only TWO sub-parts, (i) and (ii), 2 marks each — no (iii) and no internal choice; Case Studies 2 and 3 have (i)/(ii)/(iii)(a)/(iii)(b) at 1/1/2/2. SET OVERLAP: 38 of the 52 rows are questions 65/2/1 also carries, RESHUFFLED and RENUMBERED (e.g. 65/2/1's Q1 is this paper's Q13, its Q8 is this Q2, its Q18 is this Q12; case studies rotate by one — 65/2/1's CS1 is this paper's CS3). Each was confirmed on MY page and then the reference's stem/option/context LaTeX was reused byte-for-byte, verified programmatically: 38 byte-identical, 0 with drift, so they should dedup cleanly at commit. The 14 genuinely new rows are Q1, Q6, Q7, Q14, Q18, Q22, Q25a, Q25b, Q27, Q30a, Q30b, Q32, Q33a, Q33b. NOTE on plan.txt: its SKIP entry 'Q18#1 = 65-2-1 Q18#1' is a number-level mis-attribution of exactly the kind section 6 warns about — this paper's Q18 is a definite-integral MCQ that 65/2/1 does not contain, while the 30-degree/120-degree direction-cosine question it meant is this paper's Q12. Its other two SKIP entries (Q23, Q36) were correct.

questions.context:
The month of September is celebrated as the Rashtriya Poshan Maah across the country. Following a healthy and well-balanced diet is crucial in order to supply the body with the proper nutrients it needs. A balanced diet also keeps us mentally fit and promotes improved level of energy.

A dietician wishes to minimize the cost of a diet involving two types of foods, food X (x kg) and food Y (y kg) which are available at the rate of ₹ 16/kg and ₹ 20/kg respectively. The feasible region satisfying the constraints is shown in Figure-2.

On the basis of the above information, answer the following questions :
questions.stem: Identify and write all the constraints which determine the given feasible region in Figure-2.
questions._figure: REQUIRED — Figure-2 IS the feasible region and the stem names it explicitly; (i) asks the student to read the bounding lines off it and (ii) needs its corner points. Nothing in the text states the constraints. Page idx 18. NOTE: in the rendered PNG the figure panel is partly overpainted with black bars; the legible parts show corners D(0, 8), C(1, 5), B(2, 4), A(10, 0) and the lines 3x + y = 8, 4x + 5y = 28, x + 2y = 10, x + y = 6. A clean crop must come from the source PDF.
